This is a simple list of the people of the enterprise, both internal and external, which are affected by the project. The register identifies what role each stakeholder plays in the client organization, project team or suppliers to the project. The register is dynamic in that existing stakeholders may change in terms of their involvement or influence on the project.

The stakeholder register may include not only people directly involved with the delivery of the project or those that realize the benefits of the project outputs, but also any vendors, suppliers, customers, or shareholders who may be impacted by project outcomes.

A stakeholder register is not the same as an organizational chart. Instead, it identifies the organizational and interpersonal relationships of people that will affect an engagement.

The success of a change initiative is often influenced by the unofficial or unrecognized relationships that exist between principal players within an organization, or from influences outside an organization such as unions.

Much of the value of this work product comes from thinking of the project from each stakeholder's perspective and incorporating that understanding into the management of the project.

This work product is a useful onboarding reference for other project members. Keep it updated over the life of the project.

The stakeholder register is used to identify external and internal people or organizations that may influence or be impacted by the engagement, as well as identifying individuals who may be of assistance or potentially be a hinderance.

This work product typically contains the following attributes:

  • Name of individual
  • Designation
  • Department
  • Role
  • Internal/external
  • Expectations
  • Type of communication
  • Influence
